segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Kathryn and today we have an elementary level lesson about food, one of my favorite things to talk about.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们有一个关于食物的初级课程，这是我最喜欢谈论的事情之一。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We are going to talk about food but specifically we're going to talk about a family barbecue.
segments.zh: 我们将谈论食物，但特别是我们要谈谈家庭烧烤。

segments.en: Okay, what is a family barbecue?
segments.zh: 好吧，什么是家庭烧烤？

segments.en: Well, I'll just say a few words first.
segments.zh: 好吧，我先说几句话。

segments.en: A barbecue is usually something that we do outside.
segments.zh: 烧烤通常是我们在外面做的事情。

segments.en: We bring food, we play games, maybe have some drinks and a lot of the food is grilled.
segments.zh: 我们带来食物，我们玩游戏，也许有一些饮料，很多食物是烤的。

segments.en: So that's what we're talking about today.
segments.zh: 这就是我们今天所说的。

segments.en: We're going to hear this dialogue first and then we'll come back to talk about it.
segments.zh: 我们将首先听到这个对话，然后我们会回来谈论它。

segments.en: Is everything ready for the big family barbecue tomorrow?
segments.zh: 明天的大家庭烧烤准备好了吗？

segments.en: Yep, the steaks and chicken are marinated and I also bought hamburger buns.
segments.zh: 都好了，牛排和鸡肉已经腌好，我还买了汉堡面包。

segments.en: We should also cook a couple dozen hot dogs and kebabs.
segments.zh: 我们还应该烤两打左右的热狗和烤肉串。

segments.en: Yeah, good idea.
segments.zh: 嗯，好主意。

segments.en: We could put some lawn furniture outside next to the grill.
segments.zh: 我们可以把一些户外桌椅搬到烤架旁边。

segments.en: I also set up the tent outside so we can hide from the sun if it gets too hot.
segments.zh: 我还在外面搭起了帐篷，这样我们就可以在太阳太热时躲避太阳。

segments.en: Great!
segments.zh: 太棒了！

segments.en: I asked Grace to bring cups and serviettes as she is also bringing two big coolers for the beers.
segments.zh: 我让格蕾丝带杯子和餐巾纸，她还会带两个装啤酒的大保温箱。

segments.en: This is going to be a great barbecue.
segments.zh: 这将是一个很棒的烧烤。

segments.en: Oh no, it's raining.
segments.zh: 哦不，下雨了。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So probably a couple of words you didn't really understand.
segments.zh: 所以可能有几个你不太明白的词。

segments.en: So let's take a look at those now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来看看现在语言要点中的那些。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Lots of food words, Marco.
segments.zh: 很多食物词，马可。

segments.en: The first one is barbecue.
segments.zh: 第一个是烧烤。

segments.en: We were talking about that a minute ago.
segments.zh: 一分钟前我们在谈论这个。

segments.en: A barbecue is something we do usually for a special occasion or for dinner.
segments.zh: 烧烤是我们通常在特殊场合或晚餐时做的事情。

segments.en: It's a summertime thing.
segments.zh: 这是一个夏天的事情。

segments.en: You go outside when it's warm and the entire family comes and we have food.
segments.zh: 当天气暖和时，你出去，全家人都来了，我们有食物。

segments.en: Sometimes people even bring food.
segments.zh: 有时人们甚至会带来食物。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So usually as you mentioned, it's something that you do a barbecue.
segments.zh: 所以通常正如你提到的，这是你做烧烤的事情。

segments.en: You have a family barbecue.
segments.zh: 你有一个家庭烧烤。

segments.en: But it's also a verb.
segments.zh: 但它也是一个动词。

segments.en: To barbecue something.
segments.zh: 烧烤东西。

segments.en: So to cook meat on a barbecue.
segments.zh: 所以在烧烤时煮肉。

segments.en: So that's cooking meat not in a stove, not with gas.
segments.zh: 所以那是煮肉不是在炉子里，不是用煤气。

segments.en: Usually it's under a fire or very warm intense heat coming from coals.
segments.zh: 通常它是在火中或来自煤的非常温暖的强烈热量下。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And so before we cook food, usually before we cook meat on the grill, before we barbecue it, we have to marinate it.
segments.zh: 所以在我们做饭之前，通常在我们在烤架上煮肉之前，在我们烧烤之前，我们必须腌制它。

segments.en: So in this situation, the steaks and the chicken are already marinated.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，牛排和鸡肉已经腌制过。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So to marinate something or which is a verb or the steaks and chickens are marinated which is an adjective.
segments.zh: 所以 to marinate something 是动词，而 the steaks and chicken are marinated 里的 marinated 是形容词。

segments.en: So basically means that you have added spices and maybe some lemon juice, different herbs or salts to the meats in order to give it flavor before you cook them.
segments.zh: 所以基本上就是说，你在烹饪之前往肉里加了香料，还有柠檬汁、不同的香草或盐，来给它提味。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So in Indian cooking for example, you marinate with a yogurt sauce and you leave the meat in the refrigerator for a whole night.
segments.zh: 例如，在印度烹饪中，你用酸奶酱腌制，然后把肉放在冰箱里一整晚。

segments.en: So marinating or to marinate is a process to give flavor to food.
segments.zh: 所以腌制或腌制是一种赋予食物风味的过程。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we've marinated our food, our chicken, our steaks.
segments.zh: 所以我们腌制了我们的食物，我们的鸡肉，我们的牛排。

segments.en: But also we have hamburgers.
segments.zh: 但我们也有汉堡包。

segments.en: So we need hamburger buns.
segments.zh: 所以我们需要汉堡包。

segments.en: What are buns?
segments.zh: 什么是小圆面包？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Buns are pieces of bread that are for special kinds of food.
segments.zh: 小圆面包是用于特定食物的面包。

segments.en: So you have a hamburger bun.
segments.zh: 所以你有一个汉堡包。

segments.en: It's a round piece of bread and the hamburger goes on one piece and under another piece.
segments.zh: 这是一块圆形面包，汉堡肉放在一片上，再盖上另一片。

segments.en: A hot dog bun is different.
segments.zh: 热狗面包不一样。

segments.en: It's like a piece of bread that's folded and the hot dog goes in the middle.
segments.zh: 它就像一块折叠的面包，热狗放在中间。

segments.en: So bun is a special kind of bread for these kinds of foods.
segments.zh: 所以 bun 是这类食物的一种特殊面包。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So remember, if you want to have a hot dog, you need to buy hot dog buns.
segments.zh: 所以请记住，如果你想吃到热狗，你需要买热狗面包。

segments.en: So people know already that you're talking about bread.
segments.zh: 所以人们已经知道你在谈论面包。

segments.en: And if you want to buy a hamburger bread, you say a hamburger bun.
segments.zh: 如果你想买汉堡用的面包，你要说 a hamburger bun。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So hamburger buns and hot dog buns.
segments.zh: 所以汉堡面包和热狗面包。

segments.en: But after we talk about having the hamburger buns, we discuss how many hot dogs we're going to cook.
segments.zh: 但在我们谈到吃汉堡包之后，我们讨论了我们要做多少热狗。

segments.en: So the person says, we should cook a couple dozen hot dogs.
segments.zh: 所以那个人说，我们应该煮几十个热狗。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a dozen is 12 units of something.
segments.zh: 所以一打是 12 个单位的东西。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So eggs are sold in dozens.
segments.zh: 所以鸡蛋是按打卖的。

segments.en: We buy a dozen eggs.
segments.zh: 我们买了一打鸡蛋。

segments.en: We buy 12 eggs.
segments.zh: 我们买了12个鸡蛋。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Or you can say half a dozen.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说半打。

segments.en: That means 6.
segments.zh: 也就是说6。

segments.en: Half of 12.
segments.zh: 12的一半。

segments.en: But a couple dozen is usually around 24, 25.
segments.zh: 但两打通常是 24、25 个左右。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So a dozen hot dogs and they are also getting kebabs.
segments.zh: 所以一打热狗，他们也得到了烤肉串。

segments.en: What are kebabs?
segments.zh: 什么是烤肉串？

segments.en: One of my favorite foods, kebabs are sticks or skewers of meat.
segments.zh: 我最喜欢的食物之一，烤肉串是串在签子上的肉。

segments.en: So you have a very thin stick and you put the meat on it and you put that on the grill and you cook the meat on the grill.
segments.zh: 所以你有一根很细的签子，把肉串上去，然后放到烤架上烤。

segments.en: So yeah, those are very common.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，这些很常见。

segments.en: For example, in the Middle East, right?
segments.zh: 例如，在中东，对吧？

segments.en: You have kebabs, sticks of meat and also maybe some vegetables put on it and you grill them.
segments.zh: 你有烤肉串、肉条，也可能有一些蔬菜放在上面，然后你就烤了。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Very flavorful, very tasty meat.
segments.zh: 非常美味，非常美味的肉。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We should also cook a couple dozen hot dogs and kebabs.
segments.zh: 我们还应该烤两打左右的热狗和烤肉串。

segments.en: Yeah, good idea.
segments.zh: 嗯，好主意。

segments.en: We could put some lawn furniture outside next to the grill.
segments.zh: 我们可以把一些户外桌椅搬到烤架旁边。

segments.en: I also set up the tent outside so we can hide from the sun if it gets too hot.
segments.zh: 我还在外面搭起了帐篷，这样我们就可以在太阳太热时躲避太阳。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.zh: 我让格蕾丝带杯子和餐巾纸，她还会带两个装啤酒的大保温箱。

segments.zh: 这将是一个很棒的烧烤。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Alright the first word that we're going to look at is lawn furniture.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们要看的第一个词是草坪家具。

segments.en: So we're going to have lawn furniture outside.
segments.zh: 所以我们要在外面有草坪家具。

segments.en: Okay so before we even start thinking about food, we have to decide where people will sit at this barbecue.
segments.zh: 好吧，在我们开始考虑食物之前，我们必须决定人们将在这个烧烤中坐在哪里。

segments.en: And so we have to find out how much lawn furniture we have.
segments.zh: 所以我们必须找出我们有多少草坪家具。

segments.en: Furniture can be a sofa, a table, a chair.
segments.zh: 家具可以是沙发、桌子、椅子。

segments.en: We have furniture in the house.
segments.zh: 我们家里有家具。

segments.en: But lawn furniture is furniture for the outside.
segments.zh: 但草坪家具是外面的家具。

segments.en: A lawn is the green grass outside your house.
segments.zh: 草坪是你家外面的绿草。

segments.en: So it's usually not going to be made out of wood for example because if it rains it might get ruined right.
segments.zh: 所以它通常不会用木头制成，因为如果下雨，它可能会被毁坏。

segments.en: So usually it's either plastic or maybe even rock or stone.
segments.zh: 所以通常它是塑料做的，甚至可能是石头。

segments.en: Or metal.
segments.zh: 或金属。

segments.en: Or metal.
segments.zh: 或金属。

segments.en: So that's what lawn furniture is.
segments.zh: 所以这就是草坪家具。

segments.en: Furniture that is made to be outside in your backyard for example or that sits on your lawn.
segments.zh: 例如，在您的后院或草坪上放置的家具。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And so we're going to be on the lawn furniture.
segments.zh: 所以我们将在草坪家具上。

segments.en: We have the special thing for cooking meat outside, the grill.
segments.zh: 我们有特别的东西在外面煮肉，烤架。

segments.en: Okay so we mentioned that you grill chicken or you grill steaks.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们提到你烤鸡肉或烤牛排。

segments.en: But it's also a noun.
segments.zh: 但它也是一个名词。

segments.en: A grill.
segments.zh: 烤架。

segments.en: So a grill, what is that?
segments.zh: 那么烤架，那是什么？

segments.en: A grill is like a stove for the outside but instead of having electricity to make the fire we have gas or propane.
segments.zh: 烤架就像户外的炉子，但它不是用电生火，而是用燃气或丙烷。

segments.en: And this is something that we light on fire and we use coals to keep the insides very warm.
segments.zh: 我们把它点着火，用木炭让里面保持很热。

segments.en: And so this is just a way to cook meats or even vegetables outside.
segments.zh: 所以这只是一种在外面煮肉甚至蔬菜的方式。

segments.en: Okay perfect.
segments.zh: 好的完美。

segments.en: So that is a grill.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个烤架。

segments.en: And if you're going to cook foods or vegetables in this way, so you're going to grill them.
segments.zh: 如果你要以这种方式烹饪食物或蔬菜，那么你就要烤它们了。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well just in case it gets hot and you want to hide from the sun, we are going to set up a tent.
segments.zh: 好吧，万一它变热了，你想躲避太阳，我们要搭帐篷。

segments.en: Okay a tent, you can sleep in a tent but in this case a tent is just a covering outside.
segments.zh: 好的帐篷，你可以睡在帐篷里，但在这种情况下，帐篷只是外面的覆盖物。

segments.en: So maybe some cloth or some fabric that will stand over us when we sit down or want to be outside.
segments.zh: 也许是某种布料或织物，在我们坐下或待在户外时撑在我们上方。

segments.en: It's also a way to protect us from the rain.
segments.zh: 这也是保护我们免受雨淋的一种方式。

segments.en: Alright so as you mentioned a tent is something that you set up temporarily made out of cloth or plastic to protect you from the sun or rain.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如您所提到的，帐篷是您暂时用布或塑料制成的东西，以保护您免受阳光或雨淋的侵害。

segments.en: Or if you're going camping you sleep in one.
segments.zh: 或者如果你要去露营，就睡在帐篷里。

segments.en: Alright and now that they have all the food, they need cups and then they mentioned this strange word, it kind of sounds French, serviettes.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在他们有了所有的食物，他们需要杯子，然后他们提到了这个奇怪的词，听起来有点像法语，serviettes。

segments.en: So I do think it comes from the French word.
segments.zh: 所以我认为它来自法语单词。

segments.en: This is a British way of saying napkins.
segments.zh: 这是 napkins 的英式说法。

segments.en: So it's like paper for cleaning your hands and cleaning your mouth that you throw away.
segments.zh: 所以它就像一张用于清洁你的手和清洁你的嘴的纸，你扔掉了。

segments.en: Okay so you can say napkins or if you want to sound a little bit more fancier you can say serviettes.
segments.zh: 好的，你可以说 napkins，或者如果你想听起来更讲究一点，可以说 serviettes。

segments.en: And speaking of fancy, let's talk about beer.
segments.zh: 说到讲究，我们来谈谈啤酒。

segments.en: Where do we keep beer?
segments.zh: 我们把啤酒放在哪里？

segments.en: It has to stay cold right?
segments.zh: 它必须保持冷对吗？

segments.en: Right so usually you would place it in a refrigerator but if you're outside or you're going camping, you want to keep them cold or you want to keep something hot.
segments.zh: 对了，通常你会把它放在冰箱里，但如果你在外面或要去露营，你想让它们保持冷或你想保持热的东西。

segments.en: You place it in a cooler.
segments.zh: 你把它放进保温箱里。

segments.en: Okay so a cooler is a plastic bin or a plastic box that we put all of the ice in and the drinks so it's not just for beer, it's also for coke and Sprite and all these different drinks.
segments.zh: 好吧，保温箱是一个塑料箱或塑料盒，我们把所有的冰和饮料都放进去，所以它不只是用来放啤酒，也可以放可乐、雪碧和所有这些不同的饮料。

segments.en: Right so it's usually made to keep something cool but as I said if you want to keep something warm you can also keep it in the cooler.
segments.zh: 是的，所以它通常是用来保冷的，但正如我所说，如果你想保温，也可以把它放进保温箱里。

segments.en: It keeps the temperature of the foods.
segments.zh: 它保持食物的温度。

segments.en: And the nice thing is that it's not electric so you can use it anywhere.
segments.zh: 好消息是它不是电动的，所以你可以在任何地方使用它。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Alright so that's all the words for today.

segments.zh: 所以家庭烧烤和做这些事情。

segments.en: Did you do these when you were young at home?
segments.zh: 你在家的时候做过这些吗？

segments.en: Do you still like to do it?
segments.zh: 你还喜欢做吗？

segments.en: All the time.
segments.zh: 一直。

segments.en: I love barbecues.
segments.zh: 我喜欢烧烤。

segments.en: It's one of my favorite ways to eat food.
segments.zh: 这是我最喜欢的吃食物的方式之一。

segments.en: The nice thing about a barbecue is you get to sit outside and relax and there's nothing better than nice fresh grilled meat.
segments.zh: 烧烤的好处是你可以坐在外面放松一下，没有什么比美味的新鲜烤肉更好的了。

segments.en: Right, and well you have all your friends over so you're having a couple of beers and you're having some meat and it's actually a really nice way of just having something at home with good friends and family, right?
segments.zh: 对，好吧，你所有的朋友都过来了，所以你喝了几杯啤酒，你有一些肉，这实际上是一种在家里和好朋友和家人一起吃点东西的好方法，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly, and some of the most important barbecues we have are in the summer near July 4th.
segments.zh: 没错，我们最重要的几次烧烤都在夏天，7 月 4 日前后。

segments.en: And so people like to have July 4th barbecues where you celebrate Independence Day and sit outside and drink and have hot dogs and hamburgers and macaroni and cheese.
segments.zh: 所以人们喜欢在 7 月 4 日烧烤，在那里你庆祝独立日，坐在外面喝酒，吃热狗、汉堡包、通心粉和奶酪。

segments.en: Actually while I was in Chile I noticed that as well near their festivities for their independence which is September 18th.
segments.zh: 实际上，我在智利时也注意到，他们庆祝独立的节日也在 9 月 18 日前后。

segments.en: A lot of people get together and have barbecues and it's so so popular that pretty much every house in the neighborhood you can smell somebody barbecuing on the weekend.
segments.zh: 很多人聚在一起烧烤，这太受欢迎了，周末几乎附近家家户户都能闻到有人在烧烤的味道。

segments.en: You're making me so hungry.
segments.zh: 你让我好饿。

segments.en: Alright guys so if you have any questions, any doubts or if it's common for you guys to barbecue back home then why don't you send us a couple of comments at EnglishPod.com and we'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 好吧，伙计们，如果您有任何问题、任何疑问，或者你们在家也常烧烤，那么为什么不到 EnglishPod.com 给我们发几条评论呢？我们会在那里见到大家。

segments.en: Bye!
segments.zh: 再见！
